name: Photomath
line: Photomath solves the problem a learner scans. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Photomath: Photomath solves the problem a learner scans. In AMP, the learner answers, and assessment, teaching and review are continuous.
verdict: Photomath solves the math problem a learner scans or types and shows the solution step by step [1]. In AMP, the learner answers each problem, and assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: The learner answers first
reasons.body: In AMP, the learner answers every problem. Many problems need a typed number, a fraction, lines of work or a plotted point, not a choice, and answers are checked exactly. The worked steps come after the answer. In Photomath, a learner scans or types a problem, and a solution appears for that exact problem, step by step, sometimes by more than one method [1]. A review of ten common study techniques rated two as high utility: practice testing and spaced practice [14].

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. In Photomath the unit is the problem the learner brings. It solves the problem it is shown, from elementary math to calculus, and what comes next is the next problem the learner scans or types [1].

reasons.title: A hint never gives the answer
reasons.body: AMP's hint gives the first step and never the answer. An answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped and does not count as learned. A skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. Photomath shows the full solution to the learner's problem, step by step [1]. Google's help pages describe further features: animated tutorials, deeper explanations and contextual hints [2]. In a field experiment with nearly 1,000 high school math students in Turkey, unrestricted GPT-4 access raised practice scores by 48%. Once access was removed, those students scored 17% lower on exams than students who never had AI. A tutor version with learning safeguards largely mitigated that harm [12]. The study was of an AI chatbot, not a solver.

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Photomath solves the problem it is shown, so an earlier skill comes back only when the learner brings a problem that uses it [1]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [13].

theirs: Photomath is a homework app from Google [3][4]. A learner points a phone camera at a math problem, printed or handwritten, or types it in, and the app shows the solution step by step [1][4]. In its maker's words, "A solution will pop up for your exact problem" [1].

The solutions cover elementary math, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, statistics and calculus, sometimes by more than one method [1]. Photomath also offers animated tutorials, deeper explanations and contextual hints [2]. There is no course: a learner moves one problem at a time, and the learner chooses each one [1]. Symbolab and Mathway also solve an entered problem and show the steps [5][6].
credit: It works on the problem a learner actually has, and reads handwriting [1][4].
It can show more than one method for the same problem [1].

theirs: Photomath's home page says its step-by-step explanations help a learner learn as they go, and cites no study [1]. We found no entry for Photomath in Evidence for ESSA or What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [7][8].

A search of ERIC, the education research index, found two papers about the app [9]. One, from 2015, is an article on teaching in a world with Photomath, not a study of outcomes. The other, by Capinding (2023), gave Photomath to 49 eleventh graders at one school in the Philippines and compared their pre-calculus performance, self-reliance and interest before and after. It reported significant gains on all three, with no comparison group [10].

A 2026 study in Kyrgyzstan gave 80 tenth graders five digital tools, Photomath among them, for eight weeks and reported higher mastery than a control group. It did not measure Photomath on its own [11].
ours: The finding that bears most on this comparison: a review of ten common study techniques rated two as high utility, practice testing and spaced practice [14]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: Your child wants to check finished homework from a school textbook, step by step.
amp: You want your child to work each problem, with a hint that gives the first step and never the answer.
You want the program to place your child and choose each next problem.
You want every answer checked exactly, with the worked steps after it.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
You want to see a level for each part of math and the actual problems behind it.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Photomath?
questions.answer: Photomath shows the solution to a problem a learner scans or types [1]. AMP chooses each problem and asks the learner to answer it. Every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Photomath work?
questions.answer: Our ERIC search found no controlled study of Photomath on its own [9]. One study of 49 students at one school reported gains from before to after, with no comparison group [10]. We found no entry for Photomath in Evidence for ESSA or What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [7][8].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. A learner can practice in AMP and use a solver to check work from a class. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
